label: D2 rare a1->S2, largest when last trial was also unrewarded a1->S2
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (ep_trial >= 85) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (ep_trial >= 95)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (zero at D1/GO). Its magnitude is set by the rare transition a1->S2 that was just observed (this trial choice and state are observed at D2): about +0.9 for any a1->S2. It adds about +1.0 when the previous trial was also an unrewarded a1->S2, and +0.4 more when the trial before that was also a1->S2, so a streak of rare unrewarded a1->S2 trials drives it to about 2.4. It falls by about -0.8 when the previous trial was rewarded, and the response weakens late in the episode (trials 85+ and 95+). Previous a1 S2 u gives a small boost (+0.25) even on other D2 transitions. All other D2 transitions sit near zero (slightly below baseline). Observed-only terms; dev R^2 beyond timing 0.74, above the profile all ceiling (0.59). Adding the model policy logit at D2 adds only about 0.015. Hidden good state, reversals and future reward add little.

issues: The claim that adding the policy logit adds only about 0.015 is wrong. Adding the term (phase==D2)*(action==1)*(state==2)*choice to the 7 original terms raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.722 to 0.786 (+0.065). The profile already hinted at this: by itself, the D2 policy decile table scores 0.40, the best single reference cue, and D2 residuals rise steeply in policy deciles 7 and 8 (+0.53, +1.29).

The history effect sizes are overstated. Once the choice term is added, the weights drop: base a1->S2 0.92 -> 0.49, previous unrewarded a1->S2 1.00 -> 0.55, trial before also a1->S2 0.42 -> 0.17, previous rewarded -0.82 -> -0.67. So part of the 'run of unrewarded a1->S2' effect is really how strongly the agent currently leans towards a1.

The worst-fit dev windows show the history rule failing. At t32 the history is a1->S2 after an unrewarded a1->S2, so the terms predict 2.26, but the actual value is 0.04. At t35 the history is a1->S2 after an unrewarded a2->S2 common trial; the terms predict 1.01 and the actual value is 2.32. Previous a2->S2 unrewarded as a modifier gets weight +0.47, but test R^2 only rises to 0.728.

Late-episode suppression is modelled crudely. Several worst windows at t96-99 have an actual value near 0 where the terms predict 1.5-2.0. Adding (ep_trial>=98) or a linear ramp after trial 80 barely helps (0.722 / 0.788 with choice), so the end-of-episode shutdown is not fully captured.

Checks that held: the feature is zero at D1 and GO; other D2 transitions sit near zero (residuals -0.04 to -0.10 against a baseline of about 0.1); the previous-rewarded drop and the previous unrewarded a1->S2 boost both reproduce; no future variables are used. A 3-term version (a1->S2, x previous unrewarded a1->S2, x previous rewarded) already reaches 0.669 test.
